as_told.title: Chariots of the Gods: ancient astronauts started civilization

plain: The idea is that the gods of ancient peoples were really alien visitors, and their heavenly chariots were spaceships. It is linked to the writer Erich von Däniken and to sites such as Easter Island. Michels sets it out himself in an episode about mushrooms, tying it to Chariots of the Gods, the book he dates to 1968. He says its premise was "that ancient alien astronauts came down to Earth around 10,000 years ago", around the time farming began, and "taught us how to basically start modern civilization." The skeptic Michael Shermer also brings it up on the show, without a source. He lumps it in with "the ancient alien stuff" of TV, the "ancient alien gods that are actually, you know, spaceships." If it were true, humanity's first civilizations would have been a gift from outside.
